author: Blair Marnell
description:
The battle for Super Earth will be coming to the big screen, just not as soon as previously expected. Sony Pictures has reshuffled its slate of upcoming films, and the Helldivers movie has been bumped from its November 10, 2027 release date.

According to Sony, the Helldivers movie will now be released on June 9, 2028. Placing the film near the beginning of the summer box office season may be a sign of Sony's confidence in the project. However, it also raises the question of whether Helldivers' time in the zeitgeist will be over by then. Two years can be an eternity in the gaming realm, especially with live-service titles.

The original Helldivers was released in 2015, but the title that helped earn the franchise a film adaptation was
title: Sony’s Helldivers Movie Has Been Pushed Back

author: Kevin Knezevic
description:
October is upon us, which means new events are just around the corner in Pokemon Go. The mobile game is entering the second month of its Twilight Trails season with some appropriately spooky events over the next few weeks, including Zorua Community Day and a two-part Halloween celebration.

That's certainly not all that's happening this month. A variety of legendary and Mega Pokemon are returning to Raid Battles as well, while fall-themed Pokemon are taking center stage for this month's Spotlight Hours.

A few new Pokemon are also making their debut in October, including Bramblin and Gigantamax Cinderace, while Astronaut Pikachu is landing in as part of a special World Space Week event. You can read more about everything going on in the game this month below.
title: Pokemon Go October 2026 Events: Raids, Spotlight Hours, Halloween, And More

author: Blair Marnell
description:
The meaning of Resident Evil Requiem's title appeared to be self-evident when it was released earlier this year. However, Resident Evil producer Jun Takeuchi's explanation for the title from the recently published Biohazard 30th Anniversary Special may be a head-scratcher for even the series' diehard fans.

"'Requiem' isn't just a title chosen for its meaning of 'requiem,'" said Takeuchi via GamesRadar. "The spelling of Requiem (REQUIEM) contains not only the 'RE (response)' ... but also a 'Q (question).' In other words, this 'Requiem' presents both an 'answer' and a 'question.' I will explain the meaning of that at some
title: Resident Evil Requiem Producer “Explains” Game’s Title, Confusing Us More

author: Jessica Cogswell
description:
To say that this summer was packed with new releases is putting it lightly. Regardless of if you were looking for something blood-soaked (The Blood of Dawnwalker and Marvel's Wolverine both fit the bill here) or a more strategic experience, such as the one offered in Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave, there seems to be something for every type of player lately. But while we're sure you've heard a lot about Summer 2026's biggest games by this point, we're here to remind you that sometimes the best gaming experiences come from unexpected places.

A 90-minute horror game about brain mold, a heartfelt action-platformer filled with Kingdom Hearts-like visuals, and an intricate job simulator where you play an advice-dishing modiste are just a few of the games we at GameSpot couldn't put down this month. Below is a roundup of our favorite new releases from the last few months, with an emphasis on hidden gems and titles you
title: GameSpot’s September 2026 Staff Picks

description:
From its return to the franchise’s gritter roots to its overhaul of the series’ iconic systems, here’s everything to know about Gears of War: E-Day.

author: Gabe Gurwin
description:
A remake of the original Splinter Cell game was first announced nearly five years ago, and since then, we've seen exactly zero seconds of the game in action, or even a trailer. However, as we know with Sam Fisher, silence can be deceiving, and it looks like Ubisoft is actively recruiting for several roles on the project.

Spotted by Insider Gaming, job openings for a few different positions, including level designer and producer, have been posted within the last few months. This isn't necessarily indicative of how far along the project is--people are hired and leave all the time--but it does at least let us know that the project is still in active development. It's also
title: The Splinter Cell Remake Is Still Lurking In The Shadows

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
The "Xbox reset" has people wondering whether Microsoft is preparing to exit the video game business, but Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has flatly denied that the gaming division will be put up for sale.

"Xbox is not for sale," Sharma said to The New York Times. "We will do whatever it takes to set the company up for success, and we will look at the right partnerships, the right operating model, and everything needed to achieve that."

Sharma's comments come in the wake of analysts predicting that
title: Xbox CEO Insists It’s Not For Sale Amid Studio Closures, Layoffs

author: Levi Winslow
description:
Sonic has had a rough go at things lately, what with the myriad games that haven't been hitting like they used to. Sega appears to be aware of that and has acknowledged that, although the games have struggled recently, the franchise as a whole is back in the zeitgeist again--and it's all thanks to the live-action movies.

In an interview with Automaton at the Tokyo Game Show, series producer Takashi Iizuka spoke about the impact that director Jeff Fowler's three live-action movies have had on repopularizing Sonic again.

"Thanks to the movies, awareness of the Sonic series has grown, and more people around the world have become interested in Sonic as a character and i
title: You Can Hate The Sonic Movies, But They Help The Games Get Made, Sega Says

author: Cameron Koch
description:
World of Warcraft: Forever is looking to keep its secrets, as over 12,500 items in the game's files have been kept hidden from dataminers.

The WoW: Forever beta is currently in full swing, and in addition to new dungeons, abilities, and even a whole new playable race, players are quickly discovering there are tons of new items that will completely change how this old-school version of WoW is played. Whether it's items with far more spellpower at early levels or gear tailored towards professions, Blizzard is definitely mixing things up so that the game's leveling journey, and its endgame, are going to feel all new.

As broken down in detail by
title: WoW: Forever Is Keeping More Than 12,500 Items Secret

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
The Street Fighter movie is shaping up to be a love letter to Capcom's classic fighting game series, with its goofy action and costumes, but if there's one crucial element it's nailing, it's the franchise's sound. Specifically, Guile's iconic theme, which is legendary for its ability to complement anything in life. How does the movie version match up? It's not straying from what is considered fighting game soundtrack perfection, but it is adding to it with a kickass guitar solo and a few more cinematic tweaks, allowing the main theme to do all the heavy lifting. Listen to it yourself, from one of the streaming links below:

  • Apple Music
title: Yes, Guile’s Street Fighter Movie Theme Goes With Everything

author: Levi Winslow
description:
Now that development of future Halo games is being handled by Activision Blizzard's hands, some former developers of the series have spoken out to share their thoughts on the shocking but not entirely surprising mix-up. This includes the former franchise creative director, who has provided some salient advice to the Call of Duty publisher.

Frank O’Connor has worked on Halo for over 20 years, first working as a writer and community manager before serving as the game's franchise creative director from 2003 to 2023. This is a guy who knows Halo like the back of his hand, and with all that series expertise, he took to Li
title: Activision Should Hire Former Halo Devs For Next Mainline Game, Former Franchise Director Says

author: Reyna Cervantes
description:
One of the biggest surprises of the year was the reveal of Diablo V at this year's BlizzCon. Sure, we'll have to wait until 2029 to get our hands on it, but take that decade-long wait cycles for new Diablo games! 

After sharing a first look at the game, Blizzard took the opportunity to talk about the improvements they’re making to Diablo V's gameplay design based on feedback from Diablo IV. Chief among them: the return of procedurally generated dungeons and worlds.

title: Diablo 5 Seems To Be Fixing Diablo 4’s Biggest Mistake

author: Dave Irwin
description:
Renown is one of two stats needed to recruit new team members in Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave. While the Support Level requirements never go above level 3, you may be intimidated by characters who require level 10 Renown. It's vitally important to note that gaining Renown will take a lot of time. Unlike the Support Levels, each Flame Lord's campaign builds their Renown separately. This requires patience so you don't get blindsided. Seeking a short-term Renown boost may risk potentially sacrificing other rewards that are far more important.

While our Gifts Guide covers the basics of wooing each NPC to your cause, you'll still need to gain a ton of Renown
title: How To Raise Renown In Fire Emblem: Fortune’s Weave

author: Ben Janca
description:
STRANGER THAN HEAVEN is a fifty-year, action-adventure saga of men with nowhere to go and their desperate struggle to find a home.

Use extreme violence to survive, and musical talent to thrive as a showman across five cities and eras of modern Japan. Coming January 15, 2027.
title: Stranger Than Heaven – 1929 Kure, Hiroshima | Era Gameplay In-Depth Look Trailer

description:
Following an initial rollout to Xbox Insiders, the Xbox disc-to-digital program is officially available for all Xbox One and Xbox Series X users. The program allows you to receive digital licenses for a whole bunch (but not all) of your physical Xbox One and Xbox Series X|S games, and Microsoft has outlined how it works and a pretty neat trick you can use.

description:
If I can credit any video game for helping me fall in love with some of the best indie games, it’s Dead Cells. The roguelite Metroidvania blend captured my interest and stole countless hours from me, so I chased that same feeling for years, trying other indies and learning to appreciate the world beyond the triple-A hits. With Evil Empire, a developer that helped create post-launch content for Dead Cells and was founded by developers from Motion Twin, taking on a modern take on Castlevania, I was all in. Even better, you can get it at a discount before it’s even available.

At a glance, Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse looks strikingly familiar. It’s a side-scrolling Metroidvania that, in reality, doesn’t differ too much from Dead Cells or the original Castlevania games (where d
title: Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse Has Its Fangs In Me Already, And Fangfully, There’s A Pre-Order Discount

description:
I'll take a new horror game any day of the year, but I love it when a studio releases one specifically in October. author: Mark Delaney
description:
End of Abyss pulls from a lot of inspirations. It has the same texture to its creepy world as Little Nightmares, which makes sense, given the team at Section 9 Interactive includes some former creators of that series. It borrows a bit from soulslikes, with its towering bosses who pack a mean punch if you don't time your dodge-roll well. Its fixed camera angles are reminiscent of Resident Evil, especially when you can hear something monstrous in a room before you can see it. 

First and foremost, it's a third-person metroidvania in which you shoot monsters, solve environmental puzzles, and regularly unlock upgrades that enhance exploration. Some of its best parts are staples of the genre, but due to a few flaws, including one that broke my trust, and some poor blending of these influences, it winds up being an inconsistent
title: End Of Abyss Commits A Metroidvania Cardinal Sin

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description: Xbox has undergone major changes since a new leadership team took over. Under Xbox CEO Asha Sharma, Microsoft's gaming division has had waves of mass layoffs, parted ways with several studios, and consolidated its remaining developers under Activision, Blizzard, King, and Bethesda. All of this is being done to make Xbox a profitable part of the Microsoft empire and to grow its reach, but former PlayStation boss Shawn Layden has suggested that the company should "pick a lane" and narrow its focus
title: Ex-PlayStation Boss Has Some Advice For Xbox: “Pick A Lane”

author: Jason Fanelli
description:
While it already feels like it's been around forever, October 31 will mark the one-year anniversary of Riftbound, the trading card game based on Riot Games's popular League of Legends franchise, releasing in Western markets. The game has seen four set releases so far, but there's one more on the schedule, Radiance, before we hit that one-year milestone.

There are many exciting cards being revealed as we get closer to Radiance's October 23 launch, and today, we have an exclusive look at the Overnumbered variants of one of the set's most notable names. We've seen the card's base form before, but this new art is a beauty to behold.

Without further ado, here's the Overnumbered variants for Ekko, Boy Who Shattered Time.
title: This New Riftbound Card Is An Exciting Variant Of A Time-Traveling Legend

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
More than a decade has passed since The Witcher 3: The Wild Hunt first launched, and on Steam, the game is doing better than ever. With the launch of The Witcher 3 Remastered, the game has surged up the Steam charts and has reached its best concurrent players level--ever. At the time of writing, the CCU has peaked at 120,975 players, beating the previous January 2020 record of 103,329 players.

That older milestone was reached after The Witcher TV series launched on Netflix, but the new numbers have blown it out of the water. The game is also available through other PC storefronts like GOG and the Epic Games Store, as well as on PS5, Switch 2, and Xbox Series X|S, so it's likely that the total number of players is much higher. Clearly, there's still a lot people out there who are more than happy to
title: The Witcher 3 Is Having A Record-Breaking Comeback In A Very Busy Gaming Month

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
The front page of Steam has long been a hot commodity for game developers and publishers, but next year, some big changes are coming. Valve has announced that it'll be changing how it handles game discoverability during sales and promotions on Steam, as it'll be moving away from the old model of a tightly controlled page through a manually curated calendar to dynamic, personalized recommendations that'll cater to individual user preferences and their purchase history.

Historically, Valve employees selected which games got featured in a limited number of fixed slots on the Steam front page, and only a fraction of discounted games got valuable front-page visibility. According to Valve, preliminary experiments resulted in up to 10 times as many games appearing per day in the Discounts & Events section, leading to measurable increases in store page visits and wishlist additions.
title: Steam Is Finally Changing How Games Get Their Big Front-Page Break

author: Darryn Bonthuys
description:
If you thought September was a big month for new releases, then you ain't seen nothing yet. As the days tick down to the November launch of Grand Theft Auto 6, numerous games are looking to avoid being caught in the blast radius of the year's biggest release, which has led to an absolutely stacked October. Between original releases, sequels, and hot indie games, the next couple of weeks are loaded with options across a wide variety of genres and ideas. You can check out our top picks below, and if you want to see what's closing out the year, you can also read through our list of upcoming 2026 games.

Dynasty Warriors 3: Complete Edition Remastered

author: S.E. Doster
description:
Modders have recently added new ways to play 2009's Modern Warfare 2, and videos are going viral, showcasing skateboarding in this classic Call of Duty game. Mechanics from games like Skate 2 were added with mods, and players can now kickflip and grind rails around their favorite Modern Warfare 2 maps. There's also a mod that puts Call of Duty players in Minecraft's sandbox world.

As shown below in the video shared by "Chasm," Call of Duty operators are seen pulling off several maneuvers on skateboards using game mechanics from Skate 2. These stunts include faceplanting on Rust, grinding rails on Terminal, and skating through the streets of Karachi.
title: Call Of Duty Modders Add Skateboarding And Minecraft To Modern Warfare 2
